subject: Pre-audit evidence triage and scope questions (ISO/FedRAMP/SOC2)
messages:
From: Sara Bloom <sara@sageaudit.com>

Subject: Redwood pre-audit: initial evidence request and scope clarifications

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time to kick off pre-audit planning for Acme's FedRAMP readiness review. We started a quick pass on the SIG/CAIQ output you sent; to keep the upcoming audit window on schedule we need to confirm a few scope items and collect a short tranche of evidence before our pre-audit call.

Quick questions:
- Which deployment modes are in-scope for the assessment? (Hosted API only, or Dedicated/Private as well?)
- For Private/VPC customers, do you treat those as separate subservice-provider scopes or are they excluded from the Redwood perimeter?
- Confirm the target audit window (you mentioned Q4 earlier) and the retroactive sampling period we should use for log/incident evidence.

Attached is a lightweight checklist we use to triage controls (native to our audit tooling). If you can return a completed matrix for the controls listed under logging, access governance, and change management by 7/16 that will let us prioritize samples.

Best,
Sara Bloom
Principal Auditor, SageAudit

Attachments: pre-audit_checklist_template.xlsx (referenced)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2026-07-14T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pre-audit: initial evidence request and scope clarifications

Sara — thanks, attached is our triage matrix (evidence_request_matrix_v2.xlsx). Answers inline to your questions:

- In-scope: Hosted API and Dedicated (reserved capacity) are in-scope. Private (customer-managed VPC/on-prem) is out-of-scope for Redwood's FedRAMP boundary unless the customer opts into our managed private tenancy (rare). We flagged this in the control mapping snapshot (attached).

- Subservice-provider handling: For Dedicated we consider our infra and runtime as the Redwood perimeter; for customer-managed Private deployments, the customer is responsible for network and host-level controls — we provide attestations for config guidance only.

- Audit window: Confirming Q4 2026 (week of 2026-11-08 tentative). For sampling we propose: 6 months for operational logs and incidents (back to 2026-05-01), 12 months for configuration/patching evidence per ISO/FedRAMP expectations. If SageAudit recommends otherwise, please call it out.

Open clarifications we need from you:
1) Any specific FedRAMP control baselines you're targeting (Low / Moderate)?
2) Expected evidence format for KM/Key Management controls (KMS/HSM: do you need KMS config snapshots, key rotation logs, or HSM certs?).
3) Are exception/compensating control write-ups acceptable for subservice-provider gaps?

Next steps: Marissa will own evidence collation for logging and change management; Karthik will be point for infra config and quant. Soojin will compile SOC2 evidence tangential to the ISO mapping.

Priya Natarajan
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_request_matrix_v2.xlsx, control_mapping_snapshot.pdf

Date: 2026-07-14T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pre-audit: initial evidence request and scope clarifications

Looping in some tactical asks so we can triage owner-level work:

- For logging: we need to know the exact retention requirements SageAudit will test to. Priya proposed 6 months sampling window — is that sufficient for FedRAMP Moderate? If SageAudit needs 12 months for logs we should re-prioritize.
- For Dedicated instances: confirm whether we should produce per-customer control snapshots or if a toy sample customer (Acme) is sufficient. Producing per-customer snapshots is heavy; prefer to evidence at the tenant-agnostic layer if acceptable.
- For evidence packaging: do we need original syslog exports, or are filtered overlays (redacted) acceptable for sensitive PII? We have tooling that masks and exports event metadata — saves time but might not satisfy auditors in all cases.

Action items for internal owners:
- Marissa: compile sample log extracts and change-request tickets for May–Jul 2026.
- Karthik: export KMS rotation logs and kernel-level patching manifests for the same window.
- Soojin: extract SOC2 control evidence that maps to ISO/PCI/FedRAMP overlap areas (access reviews, user provisioning).

I'll coordinate packaging for transfer and sign-off.

-Marissa
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Bloom <sara@sageaudit.com>

Date: 2026-07-15T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pre-audit: initial evidence request and scope clarifications

Thanks Priya/Marissa — quick clarifications from our baseline:

- FedRAMP baseline: Acme requested Moderate. For Moderate we typically request 12 months of audit log sampling for certain controls (AU-2/AU-6 equivalents) and 6 months for incident post-mortem evidence is usually OK. So please plan for 12 months where feasible.
- Dedicated tenancy sampling: a tenant-agnostic layer is fine for controls that are implemented and enforced platform-wide (e.g., centralized auth, global patch policy). For controls that are tenant-configurable (network ACLs, customer-managed keys) we will ask for a sample customer bundle; Acme is fine for that sample.
- Evidence formats: original exports are preferred. Redacted overlays are acceptable but must include a manifest that describes redactions and a reproducible export method.

For KMS/KM controls: provide key rotation logs, IAM bindings for the KMS service account, and any HSM certificates if applicable. If rotation is handled by a cloud KMS, snapshots of the rotation policy plus attestations are fine.

I'll take your matrix and mark high/med/low priority controls and return a targeted pre-audit list by EOD 7/15 so you can focus owners. Also, please upload the evidence to the secure portal we shared earlier (we can provide a one-time intake link if needed).

-Sara
Principal Auditor, SageAudit
